sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: We begin today with the story of an economic bubble.
sentences.zh: 今天我们从一个经济泡沫的故事讲起。

sentences.en: Or to be more precise, a mania.
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，是一场狂热。

sentences.en: This mania took place in Amsterdam in the 1630s.
sentences.zh: 这场狂热发生在17世纪30年代的阿姆斯特丹。

sentences.en: Picture a city of canals, elegant townhouses,
sentences.zh: 想象一下，那是一座运河纵横、联排别墅优雅的城市，

sentences.en: and a populace obsessed with one thing.
sentences.zh: 城中百姓痴迷于一件事。

sentences.en: Tulips.
sentences.zh: 郁金香。

sentences.en: Amsterdam was the site of a big flowers market.
sentences.zh: 阿姆斯特丹曾是大型花卉市场的所在地。

sentences.en: It still is.
sentences.zh: 现在依然如此。

sentences.en: People would trade tulips.
sentences.zh: 人们会交易郁金香。

sentences.en: And there were some tulips that were especially beautiful, they thought.
sentences.zh: 他们认为有些郁金香特别漂亮。

sentences.en: And so people wanted those.
sentences.zh: 于是人们都想要那些品种。

sentences.en: And the price started going up.
sentences.zh: 价格开始上涨。

sentences.en: This is economist Robert Schiller.
sentences.zh: 这位是经济学家罗伯特·席勒。

sentences.en: And when he says prices started going up,
sentences.zh: 当他说价格开始上涨时，

sentences.en: what he means is they started going up a lot.
sentences.zh: 他的意思是价格开始大幅上涨。

sentences.en: People were getting rich trading in tulips.
sentences.zh: 人们通过交易郁金香发了财。

sentences.en: One tulip would be the same value as a whole house.
sentences.zh: 一株郁金香的价值等同于一整栋房子。

sentences.en: One tulip could hold as much value as a house.
sentences.zh: 一株郁金香的价值可以抵得上一栋房子。

sentences.en: Now historians say they've only found a few examples of this.
sentences.zh: 现在历史学家说他们只找到了极少数这样的例子。

sentences.en: But even more modestly priced tulips could sell for what would today be thousands of dollars.
sentences.zh: 但即使是价格更亲民的郁金香，其售价在今天看来也相当于数千美元。

sentences.en: Tulip.
sentences.zh: 郁金香。

sentences.en: Tulip.
sentences.zh: 郁金香。

sentences.en: Tulip.
sentences.zh: 郁金香。

sentences.en: From a distance of nearly 400 years, the Dutch tulip mania of the 1630s might seem absurd.
sentences.zh: 从近400年后的今天回望，17世纪30年代的荷兰郁金香狂热似乎很荒唐。

sentences.en: But the flowers were a way for the residents of Amsterdam to convey that they were cultured and influential.
sentences.zh: 但对于阿姆斯特丹的居民来说，这些花是展示他们有文化、有影响力的一种方式。

sentences.en: The tulips had great symbolic value.
sentences.zh: 郁金香具有巨大的象征价值。

sentences.en: They told an amazing story.
sentences.zh: 它们讲述了一个惊人的故事。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: The powerful way in which stories and psychology shape our economic lives.
sentences.zh: 故事和心理学塑造我们经济生活的强大方式。

sentences.en: How narratives affect not just the purchases we make as individuals,
sentences.zh: 叙事不仅影响我们个人的消费行为，

sentences.en: but the fate of our entire economic system.
sentences.zh: 还影响着我们整个经济系统的命运。

sentences.en: Most people think of the economy as following a set of fairly scientific principles.
sentences.zh: 大多数人认为经济遵循一套相当科学的原则。

sentences.en: I buy more if things are cheap.
sentences.zh: 东西便宜我就多买。

sentences.en: I buy less if they're expensive.
sentences.zh: 东西贵我就少买。

sentences.en: The nation's gross domestic product, or GDP, grew at a stronger than expected rate of 2.5%.
sentences.zh: 国家国内生产总值（GDP）以2.5%的强劲速度增长，超出预期。

sentences.en: Or say I run a company.
sentences.zh: 或者假设我经营一家公司。

sentences.en: I hire people if it looks like the economy is growing.
sentences.zh: 如果经济看起来在增长，我就雇人。

sentences.en: I cut back if it looks like things are going to tank.
sentences.zh: 如果看起来经济要崩溃，我就缩减开支。

sentences.en: If I run the Federal Reserve, economic indicators tell me whether to raise or lower interest rates.
sentences.zh: 如果我掌管美联储，经济指标会告诉我该加息还是降息。

sentences.en: The central bank is cutting interest rates for the third time since July.
sentences.zh: 央行自7月以来第三次降息。

sentences.en: It all looks very rational.
sentences.zh: 这一切看起来非常理性。

sentences.en: Very mathematical.
sentences.zh: 非常数学化。

sentences.en: But this picture neglects a fundamental aspect of economic life.
sentences.zh: 但这种图景忽略了经济生活的一个基本方面。

sentences.en: We live in a world of stories.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个故事的世界里。

sentences.en: The stories that we tell, in news reports, around the water cooler, in conversations with friends and family,
sentences.zh: 我们在新闻报道中、在茶水间闲聊时、在与亲友交谈时讲述的故事，

sentences.en: these stories profoundly shape the trajectory of the economy.
sentences.zh: 这些故事深刻地塑造了经济的轨迹。

sentences.en: Economist Robert Schiller's new book explores this idea.
sentences.zh: 经济学家罗伯特·席勒的新书探讨了这个观点。

sentences.en: It's called Narrative Economics.
sentences.zh: 书名是《叙事经济学》。

sentences.en: The winner of the 2013 Nobel Prize in Economics,
sentences.zh: 作为2013年诺贝尔经济学奖得主，

sentences.en: Robert Schiller says his interest in the relationship between stories and the economy
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·席勒说，他对故事与经济之间关系的兴趣

sentences.en: goes all the way back to his early college days.
sentences.zh: 可以追溯到他大学早期。

sentences.en: He was an economics major, but he took a history course that examined the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 他主修经济学，但选修了一门研究大萧条的历史课。

sentences.en: He was struck by the disconnect between the economic ideas he was learning about
sentences.zh: 他对自己所学的经济学理论

sentences.en: and the stories he read about how people behaved in the real world.
sentences.zh: 与他在现实世界中读到的关于人们行为的故事之间的脱节感到震惊。

sentences.en: People didn't sound like the people described in my economic theory.
sentences.zh: 人们的表现不像我经济学理论中描述的那样。

sentences.en: They seem to be faddish and vulnerable to crazes and new ideas,
sentences.zh: 他们似乎容易赶时髦，容易受狂热和新观念的影响，

sentences.en: and then they drop them and forget them.
sentences.zh: 然后又抛弃并遗忘它们。

sentences.en: It just seemed like there's a note of reality that has been lost when we separate out departments.
sentences.zh: 当我们把各个学科分离开来时，似乎丢失了一种现实感。

sentences.en: A history department has something to offer.
sentences.zh: 历史系有其价值。

sentences.en: So does the psych and sociology department, etc.
sentences.zh: 心理学系和社会学系等等也是如此。

sentences.en: But we tend to be, in academia, we tend to be polarized, or more than polarized.
sentences.zh: 但在学术界，我们往往趋于两极分化，甚至不止于此。

sentences.en: We tend to compartmentalize.
sentences.zh: 我们往往倾向于把知识碎片化。

sentences.en: And I've, all my life ever since, thought that I wanted to read what these other people were saying
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我一生都在想，我想读读其他人说了什么，

sentences.en: as well as what my economist people are saying.
sentences.zh: 也想读读我的经济学同行们说了什么。

sentences.en: Because, of course, they're all just different ways to understand the human condition, right?
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，它们都只是理解人类状况的不同方式，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, psychologists and anthropologists and sociologists and economists,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，心理学家、人类学家、社会学家和经济学家，

sentences.en: I mean, they're all basically trying to understand why people do what they do.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上都是在试图理解人们为什么会做他们所做的事。

sentences.en: They're just using different tools.
sentences.zh: 他们只是使用了不同的工具。

sentences.en: And political scientists.
sentences.zh: 还有政治学家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, so we need all these perspectives.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我们需要所有这些视角。

sentences.en: Don't be too compartmentalized.
sentences.zh: 不要太碎片化。

sentences.en: It may carry you for a while,
sentences.zh: 它可能会让你受用一时，

sentences.en: but if you don't know what's happening in other realms of thought,
sentences.zh: 但如果你不知道其他思想领域正在发生什么，

sentences.en: you might miss the big picture.
sentences.zh: 你可能会错过大局。

sentences.en: Robert says these realms of thought can help us decode things
sentences.zh: 罗伯特说，这些思想领域可以帮助我们解读

sentences.en: that otherwise seem puzzling about the economy.
sentences.zh: 那些在经济中看起来令人困惑的事情。

sentences.en: Take, for example, the story of a paper written by a mysterious mathematician in 2008.
sentences.zh: 以2008年一位神秘数学家撰写的论文故事为例。

sentences.en: The author went by a pseudonym.
sentences.zh: 作者使用了一个化名。

sentences.en: Satoshi Nakamoto.
sentences.zh: 中本聪。

sentences.en: Satoshi Nakamoto.
sentences.zh: 中本聪。

sentences.en: Who is Satoshi Nakamoto?
sentences.zh: 谁是中本聪？

sentences.en: Satoshi Nakamoto is a fake name for somebody.
sentences.zh: 中本聪是某人的假名。

sentences.en: He's a myth.
sentences.zh: 他是一个神话。

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't, no one knows who he is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他不存在，没人知道他是谁。

sentences.en: Some people have claimed to be Satoshi Nakamoto,
sentences.zh: 有些人声称自己是中本聪，

sentences.en: but we have not seen any definitive proof.
sentences.zh: 但我们没有看到任何确凿的证据。

sentences.en: When you ask about the creator, who created this, who invented this,
sentences.zh: 当你问起创造者，是谁创造了这个，是谁发明了这个，

sentences.en: they must be a real genius.
sentences.zh: 他们一定是个真正的天才。

sentences.en: Everyone's like, we have no idea.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说，我们毫无头绪。

sentences.en: The reason Satoshi Nakamoto created such a stir?
sentences.zh: 中本聪引起如此轰动的原因是什么？

sentences.en: This person, whose identity is still unknown,
sentences.zh: 这个身份至今不明的人，

sentences.en: came up with a new type of currency.
sentences.zh: 提出了一种新型货币。

sentences.en: Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 比特币。

sentences.en: The first successful cryptocurrency.
sentences.zh: 第一种成功的加密货币。

sentences.en: The story was that Nakamoto was able to invent a currency that could function without the help
sentences.zh: 故事是这样的：中本聪发明了一种可以在没有政府帮助的情况下运作的货币，

sentences.en: of any government, even against the opposition of any government.
sentences.zh: 甚至是在任何政府的反对下也能运作。

sentences.en: Bitcoin emerged as the digital currency that in theory could not be manipulated by a central authority.
sentences.zh: 比特币作为一种理论上无法被中央权威操纵的数字货币应运而生。

sentences.en: And it would be smart, young, cosmopolitan people all over the world who would secure this decentralized system.
sentences.zh: 而全世界聪明、年轻、具有国际视野的人们将保障这个去中心化系统的安全。

sentences.en: It's a wonderful story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个美妙的故事。

sentences.en: Especially wonderful, since nobody could figure out who Satoshi Nakamoto really was.
sentences.zh: 尤其美妙的是，没人能弄清楚中本聪到底是谁。

sentences.en: It can't be found.
sentences.zh: 找不到他。

sentences.en: No one has met him.
sentences.zh: 没人见过他。

sentences.en: How did he do that?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: It's an amazing story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个了不起的故事。

sentences.en: Robert makes the case that Bitcoin spread because it was a tale with surprise and intrigue.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特认为比特币之所以传播开来，是因为它是一个充满惊喜和阴谋的故事。

sentences.en: A genius mathematician invents a cryptocurrency and becomes a billionaire.
sentences.zh: 一位天才数学家发明了一种加密货币并成为了亿万富翁。

sentences.en: It sounds like the plot of a movie.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像电影情节。

sentences.en: If I was making that movie, one subplot I would include is the story of the singer Lily Allen.
sentences.zh: 如果我要拍那部电影，我会加入的一个子情节就是歌手莉莉·艾伦的故事。

sentences.en: I want to be rich and I want lots of money.
sentences.zh: 我想变得富有，我想要很多钱。

sentences.en: I don't care about clever.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎什么聪明不聪明。

sentences.en: Lily Allen received an offer to get paid for a performance in Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 莉莉·艾伦曾收到一份邀请，可以用比特币支付她的演出费用。

sentences.en: She turned it down.
sentences.zh: 她拒绝了。

sentences.en: That was the most momentous error you can imagine because she would be a billionaire if she had taken that Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 那是你能想象到的最重大的错误，因为如果她当时接受了那些比特币，她现在就是亿万富翁了。

sentences.en: And you hear the story and even if you don't know anything about cryptocurrencies, you ask yourself,
sentences.zh: 当你听到这个故事，即使你对加密货币一无所知，你也会问自己，

sentences.en: am I missing out by not getting in on this?
sentences.zh: 如果我不参与其中，我是不是错过了什么？

sentences.en: I mean, the story induces FOMO.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个故事引发了错失恐惧症（FOMO）。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And that's a strong emotion.
sentences.zh: 这是一种强烈的情绪。

sentences.en: It's regret theory.
sentences.zh: 这就是后悔理论。

sentences.en: People are fearful of being regretful that they missed something.
sentences.zh: 人们害怕因为错过了什么而感到后悔。

sentences.en: It hurts.
sentences.zh: 这很痛苦。

sentences.en: You don't want to look forward to that pain in the future.
sentences.zh: 你不想在未来预见到那种痛苦。

sentences.en: So you might as well try.
sentences.zh: 所以你最好还是试一试。

sentences.en: That's the thinking.
sentences.zh: 这就是这种想法。

sentences.en: What's astonishing is that the craze of a Bitcoin spread,
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，比特币的狂热蔓延开来，

sentences.en: even though very few people actually understand what a cryptocurrency is or understand its underlying blockchain technology,
sentences.zh: 尽管很少有人真正理解什么是加密货币，或者理解其底层的区块链技术，

sentences.en: but these terms very quickly became buzzwords.
sentences.zh: 但这些术语很快就变成了流行语。

sentences.en: Here's comedian John Oliver on Last Week Tonight.
sentences.zh: 这是喜剧演员约翰·奥利弗在《上周今夜》节目中的片段。

sentences.en: The problem is, there is now enough excitement around the very word blockchain that it's become a magnet for investment.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，现在围绕“区块链”这个词本身已经有了足够的兴奋感，以至于它成了投资的磁铁。

sentences.en: Reuters found that existing companies that merely added the word blockchain to their name saw their stock price on average increase more than threefold.
sentences.zh: 路透社发现，那些仅仅在名字中加入“区块链”一词的现有公司，其股价平均上涨了三倍多。

sentences.en: Robert, so you read at one point that the total value of Bitcoin exceeded $300 billion, but Bitcoin has no value unless people think it has value.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，你曾提到比特币的总价值一度超过3000亿美元，但除非人们认为它有价值，否则比特币本身毫无价值。

sentences.en: So something that existed purely in people's heads went from being worth $0 to $300 billion?
sentences.zh: 所以，一个纯粹存在于人们头脑中的东西，从价值0美元变成了3000亿美元？

sentences.en: Yes, it can easily happen if the viral effect is strong enough.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果病毒式传播效应足够强，这种情况很容易发生。

sentences.en: Now, Bitcoin enthusiasts will say, well, what about gold?
sentences.zh: 现在，比特币爱好者会说，那黄金呢？

sentences.en: Gold has no real value, just a shiny metal, pretty to look at.
sentences.zh: 黄金没有实际价值，只是一种闪亮的金属，看起来很漂亮。

sentences.en: And yet it has tremendous value.
sentences.zh: 然而它却拥有巨大的价值。

sentences.en: And it has for thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 而且几千年来一直如此。

sentences.en: But I have to say there's some differences.
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，它们之间还是有一些区别的。

sentences.en: Gold is scarce, inherently scarce.
sentences.zh: 黄金是稀缺的，天生稀缺。

sentences.en: Anybody can start a new cryptocurrency.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以创造一种新的加密货币。

sentences.en: Gold is in the Bible.
sentences.zh: 黄金在《圣经》中就有记载。

sentences.en: It's mentioned over 300 times in the Holy Bible.
sentences.zh: 它在《圣经》中被提到了300多次。

sentences.en: You know, I was thinking about this as I was reading the book.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在读这本书的时候就在想这个问题。

sentences.en: You know, when I think about real money, obviously real money, you know, has on many occasions bought me real things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我想到真正的钱时，显然真正的钱在很多场合确实为我买到了实实在在的东西。

sentences.en: But at some level, doesn't real money function a little bit like Bitcoin in that it requires you and I to both agree that the notes that I have in my wallet have real value?
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，真正的钱难道不像比特币一样运作吗？它需要你我都同意我钱包里的纸币具有真正的价值？

sentences.en: That in some ways, we both agree on the story of what the notes mean.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我们都认同关于这些纸币意味着什么的那个故事。

sentences.en: And the story is what gives the notes their power.
sentences.zh: 而正是这个故事赋予了这些纸币力量。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You've spoken just perfectly about narrative economics.
sentences.zh: 你对叙事经济学的阐述非常完美。

sentences.en: I'll give you another example.
sentences.zh: 我再给你举个例子。

sentences.en: Banks.
sentences.zh: 银行。

sentences.en: Why don't banks fail?
sentences.zh: 为什么银行不会倒闭？

sentences.en: All it takes is a story.
sentences.zh: 靠的就是一个故事。

sentences.en: If someone says the bank is going to be bankrupt soon, everybody will rush in and try to take their money out.
sentences.zh: 如果有人说某家银行快要破产了，所有人都会蜂拥而至，试图把钱取出来。

sentences.en: And the banks can't.
sentences.zh: 而银行却拿不出来。

sentences.en: They don't have it on hand.
sentences.zh: 它们手头没有那么多现金。

sentences.en: They can't pay it out.
sentences.zh: 它们无法支付。

sentences.en: So that's another example of how, yes, our whole banking system is built on a narrative.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是另一个例子，证明了我们的整个银行体系确实是建立在一种叙事之上的。

sentences.en: Yeah, because at any given point, the bank might have enough money, cash on hand, to basically pay out, you know, 5% or 10% of what its total assets are.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为在任何特定时刻，银行手头的现金可能只够支付其总资产的 5% 或 10%。

sentences.en: It's investing the rest of the money in other projects.
sentences.zh: 其余的钱都投资在其他项目中了。

sentences.en: So if everyone asks for their money back at the same time, the bank would simply not be able to deliver.
sentences.zh: 所以如果每个人同时要求取回存款，银行根本无法兑现。

sentences.en: And it happens.
sentences.zh: 这种情况确实会发生。

sentences.en: And it's supported by visual imagery.
sentences.zh: 而且它还有视觉图像作为支撑。

sentences.en: Photographers go to the bank and they take a photograph of the big crowd clamoring to get in to get their money out.
sentences.zh: 摄影师会去银行，拍下大批人群挤进去取钱的照片。

sentences.en: This has happened so many times that the FDIC, the Federal Deposit Insurance Company, has a gallery of photos in one of their residences.
sentences.zh: 这种情况发生过太多次，以至于联邦存款保险公司（FDIC）在他们的办公地点专门设有一个照片陈列室。

sentences.en: And so it's become a narrative in itself that we have to watch out for that it doesn't come back.
sentences.zh: 因此，这本身已经成为一种我们需要警惕的叙事，防止它卷土重来。

sentences.en: It's a perennial narrative.
sentences.zh: 这是一种经久不衰的叙事。

sentences.en: So Bitcoin was not just a mysterious new scheme.
sentences.zh: 所以比特币不仅仅是一个神秘的新骗局。

sentences.en: It tapped into many deep and ancient narratives about ordinary people and elites, about anarchy, about populism.
sentences.zh: 它触及了许多关于普通民众与精英、关于无政府主义、关于民粹主义的深刻而古老的叙事。

sentences.en: Talk to me about those larger themes that it tapped into.
sentences.zh: 跟我谈谈它所触及的那些更宏大的主题吧。

sentences.en: Well, there was a movement that began in the 19th century with the philosopher Proudhon called anarchism,
sentences.zh: 嗯，19 世纪出现了一场由哲学家蒲鲁东发起的运动，叫做无政府主义，

sentences.en: which took an extreme statement that we don't need any government.
sentences.zh: 它提出了一个极端的观点，即我们不需要任何政府。

sentences.en: If we just leave the people alone with no government, they will do much better.
sentences.zh: 如果我们让人们自由生活，没有政府干预，他们会过得更好。

sentences.en: People are naturally inclined, many people, to anarchism.
sentences.zh: 很多人天生就倾向于无政府主义。

sentences.en: And so they're so happy to hear Bitcoin, which was claimed can't be controlled by the government because Bitcoin is for the whole world.
sentences.zh: 所以他们很高兴听到比特币，因为有人声称比特币不受政府控制，它是属于全世界的。

sentences.en: It just sounds so enlightened and brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这听起来既开明又高明。

sentences.en: And in some ways, if you feel like you're part of the large number of people who doesn't have power, who doesn't have a voice,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，如果你觉得自己属于那些没有权力、没有话语权的广大群体，

sentences.en: and you feel like powerful elites are running your life, as many people do, in some ways, Bitcoin is, you know,
sentences.zh: 并且像许多人一样，觉得强大的精英阶层在掌控你的生活，那么在某种意义上，比特币，你知道，

sentences.en: it's sort of you're throwing a rock against the edifice of the elites.
sentences.zh: 就像是你向精英阶层的大厦投掷了一块石头。

sentences.en: You're basically fighting back in some ways.
sentences.zh: 你在某种程度上是在进行反击。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And when you buy Bitcoin, you feel like you're on the bright side of things.
sentences.zh: 当你购买比特币时，你会觉得你站在了光明的一方。

sentences.en: You're an owner of some of this fancy computer stuff, in a sense.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，你成了这些时髦计算机产品的所有者。

sentences.en: And you're part of it.
sentences.zh: 你是其中的一员。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're one of the disruptors.
sentences.zh: 没错，你是颠覆者之一。

sentences.en: You're not the ones being disrupted.
sentences.zh: 你不是那个被颠覆的人。

sentences.en: That's the hope that it gives you, yes.
sentences.zh: 这就是它带给你的希望，是的。

sentences.en: Robert says these underlying currents help explain why a story like Bitcoin took off.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特说，这些潜在的潮流有助于解释为什么像比特币这样的故事会流行起来。

sentences.en: If psychology and sociology explain the origins of economic fads, Robert draws on ideas from another field, medicine,
sentences.zh: 如果说心理学和社会学解释了经济风潮的起源，那么罗伯特则借鉴了另一个领域——医学——的观点，

sentences.en: to understand how such fads spread and when they die.
sentences.zh: 来理解这些风潮是如何传播以及何时消亡的。

sentences.en: Stories, he says, function like viruses or parasites.
sentences.zh: 他说，故事的作用就像病毒或寄生虫一样。

sentences.en: They spread only when they have a receptive hoSt.
sentences.zh: 它们只有在有易感宿主时才会传播。

sentences.en: It is really important to understand that things that are popular are the result of contagion.
sentences.zh: 理解流行事物是传染的结果，这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: There's a contagion rate, which varies through time.
sentences.zh: 存在一个随时间变化的传染率。

sentences.en: There's also a recovery rate, how soon people forget about the narrative.
sentences.zh: 还有一个恢复率，即人们遗忘这个叙事的速度。

sentences.en: This is just straight out of medical epidemiology.
sentences.zh: 这完全是医学流行病学的内容。

sentences.en: The contagion rate has to be higher than the recovery rate, and then the epidemic will take off.
sentences.zh: 传染率必须高于恢复率，疫情才会爆发。

sentences.en: It will start small, but it will get bigger and bigger, until the contagion rate falls down below the recovery rate, and then it starts to recede.
sentences.zh: 它会从小规模开始，但会越来越大，直到传染率降到恢复率以下，然后它就开始消退。

sentences.en: It's mysterious because we don't normally think about the contagion rate and the recovery rate for stories.
sentences.zh: 这很神秘，因为我们通常不会去思考故事的传染率和恢复率。

sentences.en: But that, in fact, are basic parameters that explain when they get strong and when they fade away.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，这些正是解释它们何时变得强大、何时消退的基本参数。

sentences.en: And, of course, for the people who haven't invested in Bitcoin, who didn't get in on the craze,
sentences.zh: 当然，对于那些没有投资比特币、没有赶上这股热潮的人来说，

sentences.en: those people might listen to this and say, hang on a second, I wasn't affected by the story.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会听了这些说，等一下，我并没有受到这个故事的影响。

sentences.en: But in some ways, that's not different from an epidemic.
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，这与流行病没什么不同。

sentences.en: Not everyone falls sick when an epidemic is raging.
sentences.zh: 并不是每个人在疫情肆虐时都会生病。

sentences.en: Yeah, so if you have not invested in Bitcoin, that's not necessarily a sign of your common sense.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以如果你没有投资比特币，那并不一定说明你有常识。

sentences.en: It's just that you never encountered a contagious person who's spreading the word.
sentences.zh: 只是因为你从未遇到过传播这个消息的传染源。

sentences.en: Bitcoin is a single story.
sentences.zh: 比特币是一个单一的故事。

sentences.en: When we come back, Robert Schiller makes the case that narrative economics can explain larger phenomena,
sentences.zh: 回来之后，罗伯特·席勒将论证叙事经济学可以解释更宏大的现象，

sentences.en: including shifts in the entire economy.
sentences.zh: 包括整个经济的转型。

sentences.en: Robert, in your book, you write, when we choose to tell a story to others,
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，你在书中写道，当我们选择向他人讲述一个故事时，

sentences.en: we base that choice on our perceptions of how people will react to that story in their own minds.
sentences.zh: 我们基于对人们内心将如何反应的感知来做出这种选择。

sentences.en: We will likely spread a story, whether it is a story about boomtime thinking or about economic despair,
sentences.zh: 我们很可能会传播一个故事，无论是关于繁荣时期的想法还是经济绝望的故事，

sentences.en: if we think that others will like the story enough to want to spread it further.
sentences.zh: 只要我们认为别人会足够喜欢这个故事，从而想要进一步传播它。

sentences.en: Talk about this idea that part of the reason stories spread, and some stories spread more than others,
sentences.zh: 谈谈这个观点：故事传播的部分原因，以及有些故事比其他故事传播得更广的原因，

sentences.en: is that we are actually, each of us, gauging whether if we tell the story to somebody else,
sentences.zh: 实际上是因为我们每个人都在衡量，如果我们把这个故事告诉别人，

sentences.en: they in turn would want to pass it on.
sentences.zh: 他们是否会愿意将其传递下去。

sentences.en: Right, well, it's what psychologists call theory of mind.
sentences.zh: 没错，这就是心理学家所说的“心智理论”。

sentences.en: That is, we're always thinking about what we imagine other people are thinking.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们总是在思考我们想象中别人在想什么。

sentences.en: That's because understanding other people's thinking is very important for success in human society.
sentences.zh: 这是因为理解他人的想法对于在人类社会中取得成功非常重要。

sentences.en: People enjoy conversation.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢交谈。

sentences.en: It's part of our species.
sentences.zh: 这是我们物种的一部分。

sentences.en: It's everywhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 它在世界各地随处可见。

sentences.en: Everywhere you go, you'll see people standing, facing each other, engaged in conversation.
sentences.zh: 无论你走到哪里，都会看到人们站着面对面交谈。

sentences.en: And if you get a translation of what they're saying, they're telling stories.
sentences.zh: 如果你翻译他们说的话，他们其实是在讲故事。

sentences.en: And people, when they hear a story, they turn it over in their mind and say,
sentences.zh: 当人们听到一个故事时，他们会在脑海中反复琢磨，然后想，

sentences.en: maybe I could use this story in another conversation.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以在另一场谈话中用到这个故事。

sentences.en: So people evaluate them based on their apparent success in motivating other people.
sentences.zh: 所以人们根据故事在激励他人方面的潜在成功率来评估它们。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's as if people are all trying to go viral.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，就好像每个人都在试图让自己的故事病毒式传播。

sentences.en: Well, it's not a new thing with the Internet.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这并不是互联网时代才有的新鲜事。

sentences.en: They were going viral thousands of years ago.
sentences.zh: 几千年前它们就已经在病毒式传播了。

sentences.en: Nearly a century ago, a powerful story swept the country.
sentences.zh: 近一个世纪前，一个强大的故事席卷了全国。

sentences.en: It's a story that has echoes in our own time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个在我们这个时代也有回响的故事。

sentences.en: And the lessons from history are instructive.
sentences.zh: 历史的教训是具有启发性的。

sentences.en: In the 1920s and 30s, many people feared that technological innovations were going to disrupt the economy and put lots of people out of work.
sentences.zh: 在 20 世纪 20 年代和 30 年代，许多人担心技术创新会扰乱经济，导致大量人失业。

sentences.en: For the majority, it means the interminable line outside factory gates, desperately hoping for a job that rarely comes.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数人来说，这意味着工厂大门外无休止的排队，绝望地盼望着一份几乎不会到来的工作。

sentences.en: It explains some things that got out of hand and bad.
sentences.zh: 它解释了一些失控和糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: The Great Depression of the 1930s came shortly after the term technological unemployment became popular in the late 1920s about machines replacing jobs.
sentences.zh: 20 世纪 30 年代的大萧条，就发生在“技术性失业”这个词在 20 世纪 20 年代末流行起来之后，当时人们谈论的是机器取代工作。

sentences.en: Machines replaced hands.
sentences.zh: 机器取代了人手。

sentences.en: New machines replaced old machines.
sentences.zh: 新机器取代了旧机器。

sentences.en: New inventions.
sentences.zh: 新的发明。

sentences.en: The electric light, automobile, telephone started as luxuries then as they were made better and cheaper became Conplace.
sentences.zh: 电灯、汽车、电话最初是奢侈品，后来随着制造得更好、更便宜，它们变得司空见惯。

sentences.en: And when the unemployment rate got high after 1930, people started to think, this is it.
sentences.zh: 当 1930 年后失业率居高不下时，人们开始想，就是这样了。

sentences.en: It's robots replacing our jobs.
sentences.zh: 是机器人取代了我们的工作。

sentences.en: You may think, it's pretty strange that people thought about robots in 1930.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得，人们在 1930 年就想到机器人很奇怪。

sentences.en: That sounds like long before they had computers.
sentences.zh: 那听起来像是计算机出现很久之前的事了。

sentences.en: But they did think they had robots.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实认为他们有机器人。

sentences.en: I'll give you an example of what they called a robot.
sentences.zh: 我给你举一个他们称之为机器人的例子。

sentences.en: It's the dial telephone.
sentences.zh: 那就是拨号电话。

sentences.en: Before that, when you picked up a phone, there was no dial, no keypad.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，当你拿起电话时，没有拨号盘，没有键盘。

sentences.en: You had to just, there was an operator there and it would say, number please.
sentences.zh: 你必须，那里有一位接线员，会说，请报号码。

sentences.en: Number please.
sentences.zh: 请报号码。

sentences.en: They replaced that operator with a machine.
sentences.zh: 他们用机器取代了那位接线员。

sentences.en: That's called a robot.
sentences.zh: 这就叫机器人。

sentences.en: And it scared people then.
sentences.zh: 这在当时吓坏了人们。

sentences.en: And they thought that maybe we better pull back and save some more money.
sentences.zh: 他们认为也许我们最好退缩一下，多存点钱。

sentences.en: When everybody does that, it makes the depression worse.
sentences.zh: 当每个人都这样做时，经济萧条就更严重了。

sentences.en: So one of the interesting points you make is that stories vanish and resurface, like the story you're just telling about technological innovation displacing workers.
sentences.zh: 所以你提出的一个有趣的观点是，故事会消失又重现，就像你刚才讲的关于技术创新取代工人的故事。

sentences.en: And sometimes these stories vanish and come back over decades or even centuries.
sentences.zh: 有时这些故事会消失，几十年甚至几个世纪后又回来。

sentences.en: And that really is analogous to what happens with pathogens that go dormant.
sentences.zh: 这确实类似于病原体进入休眠状态的情况。

sentences.en: And then they reemerge sometimes decades later as epidemics.
sentences.zh: 然后它们有时会在几十年后作为流行病重新出现。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A pathogen can reemerge because of a mutation, like influenza mutates quite regularly and we have to get inoculated imperfectly against those mutations.
sentences.zh: 病原体可能会因为变异而重新出现，比如流感会定期变异，我们必须针对这些变异进行不完美的接种。

sentences.en: Or it can change because of some change in our practices.
sentences.zh: 或者它可能因为我们行为方式的某种改变而改变。

sentences.en: If there's some event that brings people closer together in an enclosed space, it can spread much more rapidly and the contagion rate goes up.
sentences.zh: 如果有什么事件让人们在封闭的空间里靠得更近，它就能传播得更快，传染率就会上升。

sentences.en: So these are fundamental lessons that I don't hear very often from most economists.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是基本的教训，我很少从大多数经济学家那里听到。

sentences.en: They don't talk in these terMs.
sentences.zh: 他们不以这些术语交谈。

sentences.en: And they don't see the causal impact from narratives to the economy.
sentences.zh: 他们看不到叙事对经济的因果影响。

sentences.en: So it's interesting when we think about stories, if you draw the analogy with pathogens,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们思考故事时，如果你用病原体做类比，这很有趣，

sentences.en: perhaps then modifications to stories or tweaks in an underlying story might be necessary for a dormant story to come back and become dominant again.
sentences.zh: 也许对故事的修改或对潜在故事的微调，对于一个休眠故事的回归并再次占据主导地位可能是必要的。

sentences.en: Yes, and so sometimes the tweaks are just frivolous sounding.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以有时这些微调听起来只是无关紧要的。

sentences.en: I'll give an example from my book.
sentences.zh: 我从我的书中举个例子。

sentences.en: The idea of trickle-down economics where you cut taxes on the rich, on the theory that they will raise GDP and ultimately enrich the poorer people,
sentences.zh: “涓滴经济学”的理念，即通过削减富人的税收，理论上他们会提高 GDP 并最终使穷人致富，

sentences.en: was starting to look pretty old by the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 到 20 世纪 70 年代看起来已经相当过时了。

sentences.en: But then a new narrative appeared then, was really written by a writer, Jude Wyniski, about the Laffer curve.
sentences.zh: 但随后出现了一个新的叙事，是由作家裘德·万尼斯基关于拉弗曲线所写的。

sentences.en: And it was basically the same theory that if you cut taxes, GDP will go up and tax revenues will even go up.
sentences.zh: 其基本理论是一样的：如果你减税，GDP 就会上升，税收收入甚至也会上升。

sentences.en: You just have to cut taxes.
sentences.zh: 你只需要减税。

sentences.en: That was a lovely story.
sentences.zh: 那是一个可爱的故事。

sentences.en: And it was embellished by details, visual images.
sentences.zh: 它被细节和视觉图像所修饰。

sentences.en: It was said that Arthur Laffer, the economist, presented his idea, new idea about taxes,
sentences.zh: 据说经济学家阿瑟·拉弗在一家高级餐厅里，与国防部长唐纳德·拉姆斯菲尔德和未来的副总统迪克·切尼一起，

sentences.en: in the form of a diagram which he drew on a napkin at a fancy restaurant with Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld and future Vice President Dick Cheney.
sentences.zh: 用餐巾纸画了一个图表，展示了他关于税收的新想法。

sentences.en: Putting these names and a visual image of a diagram drawn on a napkin was all that that narrative needed to get epidemic again.
sentences.zh: 把这些名字和一个画在餐巾纸上的图表的视觉形象结合起来，就是那个叙事再次流行起来所需要的一切。

sentences.en: And that led to, I would say, Margaret Thatcher's ascendance to the prime minister in Britain in 79, and then Ronald Reagan, President of the United States, both tax cutters.
sentences.zh: 这导致了，我想说，玛格丽特·撒切尔在 79 年当选英国首相，随后是美国总统罗纳德·里根，他们都是减税派。

sentences.en: So the diagram drawn on that napkin eventually came to be called the Laffer curve.
sentences.zh: 所以那张画在餐巾纸上的图表最终被称为拉弗曲线。

sentences.en: Explain what that curve is.
sentences.zh: 解释一下那条曲线是什么。

sentences.en: Explain what the very simple intuition is behind that curve that eventually led to fairly significant policy changes on both sides of the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 解释一下那条曲线背后非常简单的直觉，它最终导致了大西洋两岸相当重大的政策变革。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's almost the Laffer curve story.
sentences.zh: 是的，这几乎就是拉弗曲线的故事。

sentences.en: It's almost like a joke with a punchline.
sentences.zh: 它几乎就像一个带笑点的笑话。

sentences.en: So what Laffer said is, if we have a 0% tax rate on incomes, how much will we collect?
sentences.zh: 所以拉弗说的是，如果我们对收入征收 0% 的税率，我们会收到多少？

sentences.en: Zero, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然是零。

sentences.en: But what if we have a 100% tax rate on incomes?
sentences.zh: 但如果我们对收入征收 100% 的税率呢？

sentences.en: What will we collect?
sentences.zh: 我们会收到多少？

sentences.en: Well, it'll be zero again, because nobody's going to work if the government takes all of it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，又会是零，因为如果政府拿走全部收入，没人会去工作。

sentences.en: So in between, the revenue has to be positive.
sentences.zh: 所以在这两者之间，税收收入必须是正数。

sentences.en: So connect the dots, and you have a hump-shaped curve.
sentences.zh: 所以把这些点连起来，你就得到了一条驼峰状的曲线。

sentences.en: That means that to raise any given amount of revenue, there are always two tax rates, a low one and a high one.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要筹集任何给定的税收收入，总有两个税率，一个低税率和一个高税率。

sentences.en: You can picture that on my diagram, which I'm asking you to make a mental image of.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我的图表上想象出来，我正让你在脑海中形成这个图像。

sentences.en: And so that's a new idea.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是一个新想法。

sentences.en: Nobody's been talking about two tax rates to raise the same revenue.
sentences.zh: 没人讨论过用两种税率来筹集相同税收收入的事。

sentences.en: It's clever.
sentences.zh: 这很巧妙。

sentences.en: It's like a stunt, a trick, the magic trick.
sentences.zh: 这就像个噱头，一种戏法，一种魔术。

sentences.en: It's fun.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: You'll know that you'll get a rise out of people if you explain it well enough and tell such a story.
sentences.zh: 你知道，只要你解释得足够清楚，讲好这个故事，就能引起人们的共鸣。

sentences.en: So it went absolutely viral, not just in the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以它彻底火了，不仅仅是在美国。

sentences.en: It's spread all over the world.
sentences.zh: 它传遍了全世界。

sentences.en: It might be hard to visualize this curve, but think about it this way.
sentences.zh: 要直观地理解这条曲线可能很难，但可以这样想。

sentences.en: As Rabat says, the government raises zero dollars in taxes when the taxation rate is zero, but also when it is 100%.
sentences.zh: 正如拉巴特所说，当税率为零时，政府税收为零；但当税率为100%时，政府税收也是零。

sentences.en: Think of what would happen if the tax rate was 1% or 99%.
sentences.zh: 想想如果税率是1%或99%会发生什么。

sentences.en: In both cases, the government would raise only a small amount of money.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，政府筹集到的资金都很少。

sentences.en: When it's 1%, a lot of people would go to work, but the government would get only a small portion of their income.
sentences.zh: 当税率为1%时，很多人会去工作，但政府只能从他们的收入中分得一小部分。

sentences.en: When it's 99%, the government would also get very little because only a few people would work when 99 cents of every dollar are taken away from them.
sentences.zh: 当税率为99%时，政府得到的也极少，因为当每一美元里有99美分被拿走时，没几个人愿意工作。

sentences.en: You can imagine the same dynamic playing out at other levels of taxation.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象同样的动态在其他税率水平下也会发生。

sentences.en: The intuitive idea here is that there can be two levels of taxation that produce the same amount of revenue.
sentences.zh: 这里直观的观点是，可能存在两种能产生相同税收收入的税率水平。

sentences.en: If that's the case, you can make everyone happy by taxing people at a lower rate.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，你就可以通过降低税率让每个人都开心。

sentences.en: You've got to give Art Laffer credit for that.
sentences.zh: 你得给阿特·拉弗记上一功。

sentences.en: It seems obvious now.
sentences.zh: 现在看来这显而易见。

sentences.en: And it had big, profound effects.
sentences.zh: 而且它产生了巨大而深远的影响。

sentences.en: It was a big epidemic in the 70s and early 80s, but it's coming back now.
sentences.zh: 这在70年代和80年代初是一场大流行，但现在又回来了。

sentences.en: Arthur Laffer is still there, and he's still gloating in his great success.
sentences.zh: 阿瑟·拉弗还在，他依然在为自己的巨大成功沾沾自喜。

sentences.en: That was the best thing he ever did in terms of narrative quality.
sentences.zh: 就叙事质量而言，这是他做过的最棒的事。

sentences.en: So is it true that Art Laffer himself has debunked the story about the napkin and the story with Don Rumsfeld and Dick Cheney in the restaurant in Washington?
sentences.zh: 那么，阿特·拉弗本人是否真的辟谣过那个关于餐巾纸的故事，以及那个关于唐·拉姆斯菲尔德和迪克·切尼在华盛顿餐厅的故事？

sentences.en: Well, the National Museum of American History in Washington was designing an exhibit on business history.
sentences.zh: 嗯，华盛顿的美国国家历史博物馆当时正在筹备一个商业史展览。

sentences.en: And they had the idea that it would be good to get the napkin.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得如果能拿到那张餐巾纸会很好。

sentences.en: And maybe, well, Jude Wieneski, the author of the story, had died.
sentences.zh: 或许，嗯，那个故事的作者裘德·维涅斯基已经去世了。

sentences.en: They called his widow and asked her,
sentences.zh: 他们给他的遗孀打了电话，问她：

sentences.en: We're looking for a napkin with a diagram drawn on it.
sentences.zh: 我们正在寻找一张画有图表的餐巾纸。

sentences.en: Can you look around his things?
sentences.zh: 你能在他遗物里找找吗？

sentences.en: And then she called back and said,
sentences.zh: 然后她回电说：

sentences.en: Yes, I found a napkin with a diagram.
sentences.zh: 是的，我找到了一张画有图表的餐巾纸。

sentences.en: So she gave it to them, and they proudly put it in their display.
sentences.zh: 于是她把它给了他们，他们自豪地把它放进了展柜。

sentences.en: You can find it searching on the web.
sentences.zh: 你可以在网上搜到它。

sentences.en: And they tell you they're very proud to have this exhibit.
sentences.zh: 他们会告诉你，他们非常自豪能拥有这个展品。

sentences.en: But there's one problem with it that a reporter later called Art Laffer and asked him about it.
sentences.zh: 但有个问题，后来一位记者打电话问阿特·拉弗这件事。

sentences.en: And he said, I don't believe that story.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不相信那个故事。

sentences.en: He said, I don't remember writing on a napkin.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不记得在餐巾纸上写过东西。

sentences.en: And moreover, my mother taught me.
sentences.zh: 而且，我母亲教过我。

sentences.en: It would be a cloth napkin at a fine restaurant.
sentences.zh: 那是在高级餐厅用的布餐巾。

sentences.en: My mother taught me not to do such things.
sentences.zh: 我母亲教过我不要做这种事。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, what's fascinating, of course, is that it's such a good story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，迷人之处当然在于这是一个如此精彩的故事。

sentences.en: And it's such a fun story that it almost feels a pity to apply the facts to it and debunk it.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个如此有趣的故事，以至于用事实去推翻它简直让人觉得可惜。

sentences.en: And that applies to conversation generally.
sentences.zh: 这同样适用于一般的谈话。

sentences.en: How many people actually fact check their stories when they tell them?
sentences.zh: 有多少人在讲故事时真的会去核实事实？

sentences.en: The Laffer curve is still being debated by economists.
sentences.zh: 拉弗曲线至今仍是经济学家争论的话题。

sentences.en: While the curve might make sense at the ends of the taxation spectrum,
sentences.zh: 虽然这条曲线在税收光谱的两端可能说得通，

sentences.en: it might not describe what people do at realistic levels of taxation.
sentences.zh: 但在现实的税率水平下，它可能无法描述人们的行为。

sentences.en: Most governments aren't choosing between a tax rate of 10% and a tax rate of 90%.
sentences.zh: 大多数政府不会在10%和90%的税率之间做选择。

sentences.en: They're choosing between 25% and 30%.
sentences.zh: 他们是在25%和30%之间做选择。

sentences.en: That means drawing implications from the Laffer curve might not make much sense.
sentences.zh: 这意味着从拉弗曲线中推导出的结论可能意义不大。

sentences.en: But in the 1980s, the story of the Laffer curve proved irresistible.
sentences.zh: 但在20世纪80年代，拉弗曲线的故事被证明具有不可抗拒的吸引力。

sentences.en: Calls to reduce taxation were buttressed by other stories,
sentences.zh: 减少税收的呼声得到了其他故事的支持，

sentences.en: like this one from President Ronald Reagan.
sentences.zh: 比如罗纳德·里根总统讲的这个故事。

sentences.en: They only know how many checks they're sending out.
sentences.zh: 他们只知道自己寄出了多少支票。

sentences.en: To showcase wasteful government spending.
sentences.zh: 为了展示政府浪费性的开支。

sentences.en: In Chicago, they found a woman who holds the record.
sentences.zh: 在芝加哥，他们发现了一位破纪录的女性。

sentences.en: She used 80 names, 30 addresses, 15 telephone numbers to collect food stamps,
sentences.zh: 她用了80个名字、30个地址、15个电话号码来领取食品券、

sentences.en: Social Security, veterans benefits for four non-existent deceased veterans' husbands, as well as...
sentences.zh: 社会保障金，以及四个不存在的已故退伍军人丈夫的退伍军人福利，还有……

sentences.en: So, Robert, tell me how Reagan's stories about so-called welfare queens
sentences.zh: 那么，罗伯特，告诉我里根关于所谓的“福利女王”的故事，

sentences.en: intersected with these ideas from the Laffer curve and eventually changed federal policy.
sentences.zh: 是如何与拉弗曲线的这些观点交织在一起，并最终改变了联邦政策的。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, Reagan was a good storyteller, by the way.
sentences.zh: 是的，顺便说一句，里根是个出色的讲故事的人。

sentences.en: So, he had a great deal of power from that.
sentences.zh: 所以，他从中获得了巨大的力量。

sentences.en: That kind of story elicits anger.
sentences.zh: 那种故事会激起愤怒。

sentences.en: And anger is a strong emotion.
sentences.zh: 而愤怒是一种强烈的情绪。

sentences.en: But the problem with that story is it's not a statistic.
sentences.zh: 但那个故事的问题在于它不是统计数据。

sentences.en: It's juSt...
sentences.zh: 它只是……

sentences.en: In fact, it's the record holder.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她是纪录保持者。

sentences.en: So, that means there's only one like her.
sentences.zh: 所以，这意味着像她这样的人只有一个。

sentences.en: But storytellers don't care.
sentences.zh: 但讲故事的人不在乎。

sentences.en: They tell anomalous and rare events as if they're common.
sentences.zh: 他们把反常和罕见的事件说得好像很常见一样。

sentences.en: And if it's contagious like that, it generates fake news.
sentences.zh: 如果它像那样具有传染性，就会产生假新闻。

sentences.en: You were talking a second ago about how President Reagan, in some ways, was a marvelous storyteller.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到里根总统在某些方面是一位了不起的讲故事者。

sentences.en: One of his stories affected not just how individuals and companies act, but perhaps even how nations act.
sentences.zh: 他讲的一个故事不仅影响了个人和公司的行为，甚至可能影响了国家的行为。

sentences.en: He liked to tell a story about the failures of communism in Soviet Russia,
sentences.zh: 他喜欢讲一个关于苏联共产主义失败的故事，

sentences.en: where people had to wait for years to get routine household services.
sentences.zh: 在那里人们必须等上几年才能得到日常的家庭服务。

sentences.en: In one joke he told to many audiences, he described a man who goes to buy a car and is told he has to wait for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 在一次对许多听众讲的笑话中，他描述了一个人去买车，被告知要等10年。

sentences.en: That this man, he laid down his money and then the fellow that was in charge said to him,
sentences.zh: 这个人交了钱，然后负责的人对他说：

sentences.en: OK, come back in 10 years and get your car.
sentences.zh: 好了，10年后回来取你的车。

sentences.en: And he said, morning or afternoon?
sentences.zh: 他说，上午还是下午？

sentences.en: And the fellow behind the counter said, well, 10 years from now, what difference does it make?
sentences.zh: 柜台后面的人说，好吧，10年后的事，有什么区别吗？

sentences.en: And he said, well, the plumber's coming in the morning.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，水管工上午要来。

sentences.en: And what is what is so effective here, Robert, is that Reagan is not saying explicitly communism doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，这里最有效的地方在于，里根并没有明确说共产主义行不通。

sentences.en: That message is embedded inside the joke.
sentences.zh: 那个信息被嵌入在笑话里了。

sentences.en: And that's the power of the story.
sentences.zh: 这就是故事的力量。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it also shows an example of the tendency for stories to go viral that are associated with a celebrity.
sentences.zh: 这也展示了与名人相关的故事往往会疯传的倾向。

sentences.en: The real author of that story is someone living in Russia, I suppose, who gets no credit for it.
sentences.zh: 我想那个故事的真正作者是住在俄罗斯的某个人，他却没得到任何认可。

sentences.en: It really goes viral when it's connected with someone that we know.
sentences.zh: 当它与我们认识的人联系在一起时，它才会真正疯传。

sentences.en: And that's just the way we are.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的本性。

sentences.en: Lots of famous quotes in history turn out not to have been first said by the famous person.
sentences.zh: 历史上许多名言最终被发现并非出自名人本人之口。

sentences.en: The famous person was quoting somebody else that he doesn't care about.
sentences.zh: 名人只是引用了某个他并不在乎的人的话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And isn't it also the case that sometimes the stories might not even be true?
sentences.zh: 而且，有时这些故事甚至可能根本不是真的，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, we don't even know whether there actually was a specific person in the Soviet Union who came up with this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们甚至不知道苏联是否真的有这么一个人想出了这个段子。

sentences.en: There have been questions raised about the welfare queen story that Reagan told, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，里根讲的福利女王故事就曾受到质疑。

sentences.en: And in some ways, once a story is traveling and it's embedded, the truth is often not sufficient to demolish it.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，一旦一个故事开始传播并扎根，真相往往不足以摧毁它。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is not a new problem.
sentences.zh: 这不是什么新问题。

sentences.en: It goes way back.
sentences.zh: 它由来已久。

sentences.en: If you turn on the news these days, there is a powerful story that's in circulation that tells us that a long period of economic expansion is soon going to be over.
sentences.zh: 如果你现在打开新闻，会发现有一个强有力的故事正在流传，告诉我们长期的经济扩张即将结束。

sentences.en: Although things may look good for now, many Wall Street analysts are concerned about the warning signs ahead.
sentences.zh: 尽管目前看起来一切尚好，但许多华尔街分析师对前方的警示信号感到担忧。

sentences.en: Recession warning light now flashing for the first time since 2007.
sentences.zh: 自2007年以来，衰退警示灯首次闪烁。

sentences.en: As a key predictor of recession is now.
sentences.zh: 因为一个关键的衰退预测指标现在亮了。

sentences.en: The bond market is once again flashing that ominous recession warning signal.
sentences.zh: 债券市场再次闪烁出那个不祥的衰退警告信号。

sentences.en: The economy could be headed for turmoil.
sentences.zh: 经济可能正走向动荡。

sentences.en: Falling 800 points.
sentences.zh: 下跌了800点。

sentences.en: It was in 3% of its value.
sentences.zh: 这是其价值的3%。

sentences.en: What do you tell people when they ask you to predict the next recession?
sentences.zh: 当人们让你预测下一次衰退时，你会怎么说？

sentences.en: And by the way, that's me indirectly asking you to predict the next recession.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我这是在间接让你预测下一次衰退。

sentences.en: My feeling is that we are at a heightened risk of a recession.
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是，我们正处于衰退风险加剧的状态。

sentences.en: And having a recession before the 2020 elections in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而且在2020年美国大选前出现衰退的可能性，

sentences.en: might even be 50%.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能达到50%。

sentences.en: You'll see clear evidence of a recession coming.
sentences.zh: 你会看到衰退即将来临的明确迹象。

sentences.en: But I can't go above that.
sentences.zh: 但我不能给出更高的预测。

sentences.en: There will be another recession.
sentences.zh: 还会有下一次衰退。

sentences.en: We know that.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这一点。

sentences.en: But the other question that people tend to talk about all or nothing.
sentences.zh: 但人们倾向于讨论的另一个问题是非黑即白。

sentences.en: Will we or will we not have a recession?
sentences.zh: 我们到底会不会经历衰退？

sentences.en: The question is, if there is another question, which I'd like to entertain, if there is a
sentences.zh: 问题是，如果还有另一个问题，我想探讨一下，如果真的发生了

sentences.en: recession, is there a chance that it will develop into a severe recession?
sentences.zh: 衰退，它有没有可能演变成严重的衰退？

sentences.en: And I'm worried about that, even though I can't tell you precisely whether we'll be in a recession.
sentences.zh: 我很担心这一点，尽管我无法确切告诉你我们是否会陷入衰退。

sentences.en: And I think there are narratives today that might worsen a recession.
sentences.zh: 我认为当今的一些叙事可能会加剧衰退。

sentences.en: Notably, the artificial intelligence narrative, which in an earlier form in the Great Depression
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是人工智能叙事，它在大萧条时期的早期形式，

sentences.en: really did heighten the impact of the Depression.
sentences.zh: 确实加剧了大萧条的影响。

sentences.en: We could see that again, people becoming conservative in their expenditure because they're
sentences.zh: 我们可能会再次看到这种情况，人们因为害怕失业而变得保守，

sentences.en: afraid of losing their jobs.
sentences.zh: 缩减开支。

sentences.en: I mean, it's already going on in some parts of the country, but it could become big.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种情况在全国部分地区已经发生了，但可能会变得规模更大。

sentences.en: One point that Robert makes is that the veracity of economic narratives is not the point.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特提出的一个观点是，经济叙事的真实性并不是重点。

sentences.en: Stories can invent their own reality.
sentences.zh: 故事可以创造它们自己的现实。

sentences.en: One example he gives is the narrative around Japan's lost decade, a period of economic stagnation
sentences.zh: 他给出的一个例子是关于日本“失去的十年”的叙事，那是一段经济停滞时期，

sentences.en: during the 1990s and early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 发生在20世纪90年代和21世纪初。

sentences.en: The lost decade story for Japan was particularly impactful since it followed the 1980s when Japan
sentences.zh: 日本“失去的十年”的故事之所以影响巨大，是因为它紧随20世纪80年代之后，当时日本

sentences.en: was considered the economic powerhouse of the world.
sentences.zh: 被认为是世界的经济强国。

sentences.en: People were saying that nobody can compete with Japan.
sentences.zh: 人们当时说没人能与日本竞争。

sentences.en: They've pushed out Western makers of cameras, stereo equipment.
sentences.zh: 他们挤走了西方的相机和音响设备制造商。

sentences.en: They're hammering away at their sales of cars.
sentences.zh: 他们正在猛烈冲击汽车销售市场。

sentences.en: There were books written back then about the Japanese miracle.
sentences.zh: 当时还有人写书讲述“日本奇迹”。

sentences.en: And then suddenly it went sour in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 然后到了90年代，情况突然变糟了。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if President Donald Trump might be a fan of your book, whether or not he's actually
sentences.zh: 我在想唐纳德·特朗普总统是否可能是你这本书的粉丝，无论他是否真的

sentences.en: read it, because he clearly also believes in the power of stories.
sentences.zh: 读过它，因为他显然也相信故事的力量。

sentences.en: Here he is talking down the risks of an impending recession.
sentences.zh: 他现在正在淡化即将到来的衰退风险。

sentences.en: I don't think we're having a recession.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们会陷入衰退。

sentences.en: We're doing tremendously well.
sentences.zh: 我们做得非常好。

sentences.en: Our consumers are rich.
sentences.zh: 我们的消费者很富有。

sentences.en: I gave a tremendous tax cut, and they're loaded up with money.
sentences.zh: 我实施了巨大的减税，他们手里有很多钱。

sentences.en: They're buying.
sentences.zh: 他们正在消费。

sentences.en: I saw the Walmart numbers.
sentences.zh: 我看到了沃尔玛的数据。

sentences.en: They were through the roof just two days ago.
sentences.zh: 就在两天前，数据高得惊人。

sentences.en: That's better than any poll.
sentences.zh: 那比任何民调都好。

sentences.en: That's better than any economiSt.
sentences.zh: 那比任何经济学家都强。

sentences.en: So, Robert, given what you say about how talk can shape economic reality, is President Trump
sentences.zh: 那么，罗伯特，鉴于你所说的谈话如何塑造经济现实，特朗普总统

sentences.en: absolutely right to be spinning a positive story?
sentences.zh: 通过渲染积极的故事来引导舆论，这样做绝对正确吗？

sentences.en: Well, I wouldn't use the word absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不会用“绝对正确”这个词。

sentences.en: That's a little strong.
sentences.zh: 这有点言过其实了。

sentences.en: But he is having an impact, I believe.
sentences.zh: 但我相信，他确实产生了影响。

sentences.en: It's not just his current spinning of the story.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是他目前渲染故事的方式。

sentences.en: He's written many books with co-authors.
sentences.zh: 他曾与人合著过许多书。

sentences.en: These books have advice to be like him.
sentences.zh: 这些书里有关于如何像他一样行事的建议。

sentences.en: He tells you how he did it.
sentences.zh: 他告诉你他是怎么做到的。

sentences.en: He tells you, for example, don't be afraid to boast about yourself.
sentences.zh: 例如，他告诉你，不要害怕吹嘘自己。

sentences.en: Because, you know, people are maybe a little resentful about boasting people, but in the
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，人们或许会对吹嘘的人感到有些反感，但从

sentences.en: long run, they believe in them.
sentences.zh: 长远来看，他们还是会相信这些人。

sentences.en: Because if you don't boast, nobody will hear about your successes.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你不吹嘘，就没人会知道你的成功。

sentences.en: This is Donald Trump talking.
sentences.zh: 这是唐纳德·特朗普的原话。

sentences.en: He's telling you to spread your personal narrative aggressively.
sentences.zh: 他是在告诉你积极地传播你的个人叙事。

sentences.en: And he's been doing that for himself for 50 years.
sentences.zh: 而他本人已经这样做了50年。

sentences.en: Robert Schiller won the 2013 Nobel Prize in Economics.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·席勒获得了2013年诺贝尔经济学奖。

sentences.en: He's the author of Narrative Economics, How Stories Go Viral and Drive Major Economic Events.
sentences.zh: 他是《叙事经济学：故事如何传播并驱动重大经济事件》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Robert, thank you for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特，感谢你今天参加《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Junko, thanks.
sentences.zh: 顺子，谢谢你。

sentences.en: It was a pleasure.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来。

sentences.en: This week's episode was produced by Thomas Liu and edited by Jenny Schmidt and Tara Boyer.
sentences.zh: 本周的节目由托马斯·刘制作，珍妮·施密特和塔拉·博耶编辑。

sentences.en: Our team includes Parth Shah, Raina Cohen, and Laura Querell.
sentences.zh: 我们的团队成员包括帕斯·沙阿、雷娜·科恩和劳拉·奎雷尔。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Remco Svetslout and Laura Beltran-Viamitzar.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢雷姆科·斯维茨劳特和劳拉·贝尔特兰-维亚米扎尔。

sentences.en: Our unsung hero for this episode is Christian Kutten.
sentences.zh: 本期节目的幕后英雄是克里斯蒂安·库滕。

sentences.en: Christian is NPR's financial controller.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安是NPR的财务总监。

sentences.en: He and the talented accounting team at NPR make sure that bills get paid, revenues get collected,
sentences.zh: 他和NPR才华横溢的会计团队确保账单得到支付，收入得到回收，

sentences.en: and the organization follows tax and accounting rules.
sentences.zh: 并确保组织遵守税务和会计规则。

sentences.en: Christian has helped me on many occasions think through the financial models for Hidden Brain
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂安曾在许多场合帮助我思考《隐藏的大脑》的财务模型

sentences.en: and the implications of different choices.
sentences.zh: 以及不同选择所带来的影响。

sentences.en: He's great at seeing the stories behind the numbers
sentences.zh: 他非常擅长洞察数字背后的故事，

sentences.en: and finding ways to tell those stories eloquently.
sentences.zh: 并能找到以雄辩的方式讲述这些故事的方法。

sentences.en: Thank you, Christian.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，克里斯蒂安。

sentences.en: For more Hidden Brain, you can follow us on Facebook and Twitter.
sentences.zh: 想了解更多《隐藏的大脑》内容，请在Facebook和Twitter上关注我们。

sentences.en: If you like this episode, please be sure to share it with a friend.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这期节目，请务必分享给朋友。

sentences.en: It sounded like you have a fun show.
sentences.zh: 听起来你们的节目很有趣。

sentences.en: I like it.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢。

sentences.en: It is a fun show.
sentences.zh: 这确实是个有趣的节目。

sentences.en: You should subscribe, Robert.
sentences.zh: 你应该订阅一下，罗伯特。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Take care.
sentences.zh: 保重。

sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆，这里是NPR。
